pages.text: Leo the know-it-all fox flicked a spine on Soso's back with his finger. Soso the quiet hedgehog curled into a ball. Leo laughed. "Curled again!"
Today Soso wore a new orange ribbon and planned to make flower necklaces on the grass. The words "Don't..." wouldn't come out. Soso stayed curled and still.
This time Leo pulled hard on the ribbon end. "Why is it so long?" Soso curled tighter, thinking only, 'I don't like it. I don't like it.'
Snap! The ribbon tore. A piece of orange ribbon fell into Soso's hand. "Huh? It wasn't me," said Leo, running up the slope.
Soso sat alone on the grass, holding the torn ribbon. The flowers stayed untouched. Not one necklace was made. The sun nearly touched the peak.
Grandma Bear sat beside Soso and spread the torn ribbon on her lap. "Did you dislike that earlier, Soso?" Soso gave a tiny nod.
"Leo has to hear that you don't like it." Grandma held out her palm. Soso slapped hands with her and practiced, softly once, loudly once. "Don't like it? Say no!"
The next day on the grass, Leo raised his finger again. Soso straightened from their curl and looked into his eyes. "I don't like it! Stop!" Leo's hand stopped right there.

Leo folded his ears. "Sorry. I didn't know you disliked it." Soso taught him three things. "One, stand straight! Two, look in the eyes! Three, say no loudly!" They sat side by side, picking flowers and threading necklaces.
Grandma tied the torn ribbon again and hugged Soso's shoulders. Without words, nobody knows. Say it, and they stop right there. "Don't like it? Say no!" Wearing a flower necklace, Soso grinned.
